cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Make It Official
cards.instruction: Recruit someone by giving them a title, role, or ceremonial duty that makes participation feel binding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Would you be honorary patron of our roof appeal? You'd open it and thank the donors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can come, but I won't make a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Then accept the patron's ribbon and lead the applause. That can be your ceremonial duty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I leave after the first donation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The patron applauds every donor. We couldn't have the later ones thinking their money mattered less.

mechanism: A teaches ceremonial participation that fits a reluctant patron's boundary, then makes consistent treatment of donors bind them to stay.
confusable: D170 holds for a finite ending ritual; D175 recruits and binds through the assigned honor and duty.
comparison: A negotiated public role differs from a surprise appointment after a trivial favor.
seedUse: Keep no-speech accommodation and first-donation exit; make A correct applause practice rather than merely describe the role.
